newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends above 6,800, bonds edge up, dollar rallies.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends above 6,800, bonds edge up, dollar rallies.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average closed above 6,800 points for the first time Friday, scoring a fourth record for the week, while bonds edged higher.
The dollar rose broadly, setting a near 31-month high against the German mark, as strong overseas trade and manufacturing data highlighted a vigorous U.S. economy.
The Nasdaq Composite, Standard & Poor's 500 and New York Stock Exchange indexes also finished at new highs.
The Dow ended up 67.73 points at 6,833.10, beating Thursday's record of 6,765.37. Just 12 trading sessions into the New Year, the index is up nearly 385 points, or a sizzling 6 percent.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,464 to 984 on heavy volume of 532 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said that stable interest rates and sheer momentum also propelled the markets.
"Today was a combination of factors and momentum was as much of it as anything else," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney.
"A lot of the key economic numbers are behind us which leaves earnings in control of the market," he said. "And earnings have been so far, so good."

With the earnings reporting season just a few days old, the profit reports have proven favourable and, in the meantime, the bond market has found stable footing, leaving little in the way of a stock market that continues to draw on a seasonal cash infusion and seems intent on climbing.
Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd., said, "7,000 is a foregone short-term conclusion given the behaviour of this market."
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 1/32 of a point, or 31 cents on a $1,000 bond, leaving its yield unchanged at Thursday's close of 6.83 percent.
Only a handful of companies reported their quarterly results, but among the session's standouts were several who did so late Thursday.

After the market closed, Microsoft Corp. said it earned $741 million in the latest quarter, compared with $575 million a year earlier. The per share earnings of 57 cents beat Wall Street estimates and were up from 45 cents a year earlier.

The dollar peaked at 1.6190 marks in late trading before ending at 1.6182 marks, up sharply from 1.5945 marks Thursday. The dollar also touched a new 32-month high against the Swiss franc at 1.40 before closing at 1.3993 Swiss francs, up from 1.3767 on Thursday.
The dollar rose to 117.37 Japanese yen from 116.54 yen, buoyed by the report that showed the November U.S. trade deficit with Japan shrank 12.9 percent to $4.32 billion.
Oil prices fell despite a brutal cold snap in the Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, as supplies were now seen as adequate to prevent any shortages.
"Despite the colder weather, the physical supply appears to be adequate," said William Brown of trading firm W.H. Brown in New York.

On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February heating oil ended down 1.48 cents at 68.44 cents a gallon. February gasoline ended down 0.60 cent a gallon at 68.09 cents and February crude down 11 cents at $25.41 a barrel.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index ended above 4,200 for the first time, up 10.2 points at 4,207.7 for a rise of 151.10 on the week. In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 average, which rose over 300 points early in the afternoon, ended down 54.30 points at 18,090.04 for a gain of 786.49 on the week.
